title: Raise logit softcap 15 -> 30
description: One line in GPT.forward: softcap = 15 -> 30, doubling the attainable logit range. Nothing else touched.
reflection: NEGATIVE, and by a clear margin: val_bpb 0.990289 vs baseline 0.986277, i.e. +0.0040, about 4.5x the ~0.0009 noise floor. Zero confound, exactly as predicted: params 71.3M, peak VRAM 32.9GB, FLOPs/token unchanged, and the run actually got slightly MORE compute than the baseline (333.6M tokens / 2545 steps / MFU 38.72% vs 331.5M / 2529 / 38.5%). So the whole gap is quality per token. My premise was wrong in an informative way. I argued softcap only binds late and is therefore a pure tax on a converged model's confidence. The measurement says the opposite: s=15 is not a stability guard that happens to clip, it is an active part of the loss geometry. tanh(z/s) scales the logit gradient by sech^2(z/s); a tight cap damps gradients on already-confident tokens and keeps the optimizer working on the uncertain ones. Relaxing to 30 lets easy, high-confidence tokens keep pulling on lm_head and wte late in training, which is wasted capacity. So this axis is real and it has a gradient -- it just points the other way. The cheap follow-up, if anyone wants it, is softcap 15 -> 10; it costs nothing, is a one-character change, and the sign of this result says tighter is the direction with upside. I would NOT buy 30 or removal, both are now measured or dominated. Axis status after 6 rounds: batch flat, head split negative, depth positive-but-exhausted, width flat, FLOP-free embedding capacity negative, looser softcap negative. Untouched regions left: the attention window pattern (SSSL / short=seq/2) and the LR schedule shape (WARMUP_RATIO=0, WARMDOWN_RATIO=0.5).
